items.name: source-driven-development
items.author: addyosmani
items.description: Ensure every framework-specific implementation decision is grounded in the latest official documentation with explicit citations.
items.summary: The source-driven-development skill requires every framework-specific code decision to be backed by official documentation rather than implementation from memory. Training data goes stale, APIs get deprecated, and best practices evolve, so the skill ensures users receive code they can trust with traceable authoritative sources. Use when building boilerplate or patterns that will propagate across a project, when the user asks for verified or documented implementation, or when framework-recommended approaches matter for forms, routing, data fetching, state management, or auth. Skip for version-agnostic edits like renaming variables, fixing typos, or pure logic unrelated to framework APIs. Also skip when the user explicitly prioritizes speed over verification. The workflow emphasizes looking up official docs, citing sources visible to the user, and avoiding outdated patterns. Use when correctness depends on current framework documentation.
highlights: Every framework decision must cite official documentation.
Avoid implementing framework APIs from stale training memory.
Targets forms, routing, data fetching, state, and auth patterns.
Skip for version-agnostic refactors and pure logic changes.
User-visible source citations for verifiable implementation.

items.name: marketing-loops
items.author: coreyhaines31
items.description: Turns repetitive marketing tasks into scheduled, always-on loops an agent runs on a cadence, with triggers, verification, and stopping conditions to protect rankings, retention, and revenue.
items.summary: marketing-loops helps set up repeatable marketing workflows an AI agent runs on a schedule, each with a trigger, bounded steps, self-check, and explicit stop condition. It is the operational counterpart to marketing-ideas: ideas cover one-off experiments while loops define what to keep doing on cadence by wiring other marketing skills together. The workflow reads product marketing context if present, clarifies the outcome to protect, picks or adapts a loop from references/loop-catalog.md, tunes cadence to signal speed, confirms human checkpoints via loop-guardrails.md, and schedules execution. Every loop documents nine parts: check cadence, acts-when condition, purpose, skills used, loop body, self-check, state and idempotency, stop or bail-out, and output destination. The cadence rule maps rankings to weekly checks, ad fatigue to every two or three days, churn signals to daily triggers, and content decay to monthly review. It warns against vanity loops, auto-publishing without guardrails, and over-frequent checks that train teams to ignore output.
highlights: Defines nine-part loop anatomy including self-check, state, and stop conditions.
Cadence rule matches check frequency to how fast each marketing signal changes.
Orchestrates other marketing skills from references/loop-catalog.md on schedule.
Separates check cadence from acts-when action conditions to avoid spam.
Requires human checkpoints before publish or spend actions without explicit guardrails.
